solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tight girdles might lace up without flapping

indicators.note: to girdle is to encircle, so the friendly word goes round the other letters

parts.note: tight friends are pally, close and chummy

indicators.note: up in the sense of stirred or disturbed, so the letters of might lace are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Tightly laced corsets might do up so firmly that nothing wobbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' signals the anagram of MIGHT LACE, giving HLEGMATIC, which PALLY ('Tight', as in close friends) 'girdles'.
explanation.definitionFit: A phlegmatic person stays calm and unruffled, so acting that way is doing things without getting in a flap.

clue.text: Soldier on favoured fortification

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a pet pupil or project is the favoured one

explanation.surface: A soldier carries on along a fortified position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier on' looks like the phrase meaning persevere; here 'on' just places the soldier first.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a protective wall or rampart along the top of a fortified position.

clue.text: The fleeting rain turned severe

indicators.note: turned in the sense of twisted round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Brief rain that suddenly turned into a severe storm.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or injury called severe in the gravest sense is one that could cost someone their life.

clue.text: One of brothers reported ill

indicators.note: reported as in spoken of, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm were the brothers who collected fairy tales

explanation.surface: News arrives that one of the brothers has fallen ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill in the sense of bad or ominous, as in ill tidings, matches a bleak, forbidding outlook.

clue.text: Oriental textbook I exchanged for a yen

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out and a different one put in its place

parts.note: the I Ching is the ancient Chinese Book of Changes

explanation.surface: Someone swaps an Eastern book for Japanese currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like the currency; it is the definition, a longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a yearning or longing, and an aching is that same craving, used as a noun.

clue.text: Remarkable home looking like a church

parts.note: in means at home
having a spire, as many churches do

explanation.surface: An estate agent describes a striking house built like a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A remarkable performance is brilliant, as though driven by genius or divine prompting.

clue.text: A king strangled by a savage is grasping

indicators.note: strangling means gripping round the neck, so one part is wrapped by the other

parts.note: a vicious attack is a savage one
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A monarch is throttled by a brute who wants his wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'a' joins the savage as A VICIOUS; the first 'A' and the king, AR, go inside VICIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping means greedy for wealth, which is exactly what avarice describes.

clue.text: Busy venue in Bristol harbours area needing many workers

indicators.note: harbours as in shelters, so the letter is held inside
busy as in bustling and agitated, so these letters are stirred about

explanation.surface: A bustling venue by Bristol's docks needs plenty of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbours' looks like the docks of Bristol; it is the containment signal, putting A inside the anagram of VENUE IN BRISTOL.
explanation.definitionFit: An industry is called this when its work relies on human effort more than machines, so it needs a large workforce.

clue.text: Welsh, for example, Frenchman's acquired

indicators.note: the Frenchman has acquired something, so it goes inside him

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A Frenchman has picked up a Welsh accent, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' looks like the nationality; it is the verb welsh, to break a promise or fail to pay a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh on a deal is to go back on it, the same as backing out of a promise.

clue.text: Dashing miles around, fellow is hot

indicators.note: around in the sense of turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: miles away means far off
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A dashing man runs miles and is hot from the effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miles' wants to be M, the usual abbreviation; here it means a long way off, and 'around' turns that word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing can mean rakish and flamboyant, a stylish but slightly disreputable air.

clue.text: Clumsily shift rock trapping doctor

indicators.note: the rock traps the doctor, holding those letters inside

parts.note: shale is a soft layered rock
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: Someone awkwardly shifts a boulder that has pinned a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To shamble is to walk or move in an awkward, shuffling, ungainly way.

clue.text: Obviously having lost half crown

indicators.note: only the first half of the word survives, the back four letters gone

parts.note: patently means obviously, plainly

explanation.surface: A monarch's crown, clearly, has lost half its jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crown' suggests royalty; here it means the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of the head is its top, an old word for which is the pate.

clue.text: Novel unidentified after edition's lost for perpetuity

indicators.note: novel in the sense of new and different, so the remaining letters are given a fresh order
lost means removed from the word

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for edition; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An anonymous novel survives forever after its edition goes out of print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes ED from UNIDENTIFIED, and 'Novel' rearranges the remaining UNINTIFIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpetuity is endless time, and infinitude is boundlessness, a state with no end.

clue.text: Boss died in mountainous region climbing about

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means going upwards, so the letters are read backwards
in places the died letter within the region's name

parts.note: the Tirol is the Alpine region of Austria and Italy
over means about, as in arguing over something

explanation.surface: A boss perished in the Alps while climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D into TIROL to make TIDROL, and 'climbing' reverses that to LORDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To boss people is to domineer over them, behaving like an overbearing master.

clue.text: Sloth audibly rushed by

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: tore means rushed, as in tore down the road; per means by, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A sloth can be heard as something hurries past it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the animal; it is laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is laziness or sluggishness, an inert state of inactivity.

clue.text: Having opened present, European fool's showing possession

indicators.note: the European and fool have opened up the gift and gone inside it

parts.note: to present is to give
a nit is a fool, nitwit; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A European fool shows off what he owns after unwrapping a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing possession' looks like a description; it is the grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the possessive case, as in John's book, is called by this name.

clue.text: Mischief off lad

parts.note: going off means leaving, so off means going
a son is a lad

explanation.walkthrough: 'off lad' reads like a lad leaving, but each word gives its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief or shenanigans are underhand happenings, often of a suspect kind.

clue.text: Mean bear

definitions.meaning: to signify, as an initial signifies a name
to tolerate or put up with

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb signifies something, as letters do a name, and also tolerates, as in I won't put up with it.

clue.text: Reliability with which liar could produce fairy tales

indicators.note: the stated word plus the answer could be rearranged to produce the longer phrase

explanation.surface: How trustworthy is a liar who turns out fairy tales?
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LIAR together with the answer rearrange to make FAIRY TALES; take LIAR out to leave SAFETY.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety in the sense of dependability, as with a machine that can be trusted not to fail.

clue.text: Disappointed Democrat on channel cut short

indicators.note: on means after, so the Democrat comes after
the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: a gutter is a channel for water

explanation.surface: A Democrat is let down after his channel's show is axed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the last letter, R, from GUTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutted is British slang for bitterly let down or devastated.

clue.text: Policemen addressed protest

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
a letter addressed to someone is sent

explanation.surface: Officers send a letter of complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to object, and dissent is open disagreement.

clue.text: African sots maligned, both half-cut

indicators.note: each word is cut to its first half

explanation.surface: Drunkards from Africa slandered while both were tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' looks like slang for drunk, fitting the sots; it takes the first half of each word, SO and MALI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somali is a person from Somalia in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Railway cargo in it's effectively not fully reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed read as re-viewed, looked at backwards
only part of these words is used, the letters run across them

explanation.surface: Railway freight is effectively going unchecked.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters GOINITSEFF run through 'cargo in it's effectively' and 'reviewed' reads them backwards. The Ffestiniog is a narrow-gauge heritage railway in North Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ffestiniog Railway is a historic narrow-gauge line in Snowdonia, Wales.

clue.text: People that would be noble in bars

definitions.text: People that would be noble in bars

parts.words: People that would be noble in bars
parts.note: these folk, placed inside the word bars, would become a titled noblewoman

explanation.surface: Folk who would pass for aristocrats in the pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the answer inside BARS and you get BARONESS, a noble; 'bars' looks like pubs but is a word to hold the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ones is used for people, as in the little ones or loved ones.

clue.text: 1 lower than 100 is something like 99

indicators.note: in a down entry the lower piece comes after

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
one written as a word

explanation.surface: A sum that looks wrong: one less than a hundred is ninety-nine.
explanation.walkthrough: A 99 is a British ice-cream cone with a chocolate Flake stuck in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A 99 is a soft ice cream served in a wafer cornet, an example of the edible holder.

clue.text: Magpies nested late today

indicators.note: nested as in settled into new places, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: this evening, shortened to this eve

explanation.surface: Magpies settled into their nests late this afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magpies' looks like the birds; it means people who steal. 'nested' rearranges THIS EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A magpie is figuratively a person who pilfers, after the bird's habit of collecting shiny objects.

clue.text: One ousting fifty in Anglo-Zulu fighting, English struggle

indicators.note: fighting as in thrashing about, so the letters are scrambled
ousting means displacing, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: taken as written
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: In the Anglo-Zulu war, the English struggled to drive out fifty of the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting' swaps L for I in ANGLOZ to make ANGIOZ, which 'fighting' rearranges to AGONIZ.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonize is to struggle mentally, wrestling with a hard decision.

clue.text: Promotion time after chief is cornered by mature workers

indicators.note: the time comes after the rest
cornered means trapped, so these letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: to mature is to age
grand means chief, as in grand master
men are workers

explanation.surface: A chief earns a promotion after being cornered by veteran staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion as in enhancement of power or status, the act of making greater.
